notes: Verified against the source on 2026-11-19. The post is a pre-launch design overview written in the future tense; it reports no independent verification. Where the source documents a gap, partial is accepted alongside enforced.

promises.why: Request data is used only for the request. The Secure Enclave rotates the data volume's keys at every reboot and never persists them (cryptographic erasure); the inference process deletes request data on completion.
No remote shell, no interactive debugging, Developer Mode can't be enabled, Code Signing blocks extra code, and only pre-specified, audited logs can leave a node.

OHTTP relay hides the source IP, blind-signature credentials, no user identifiers in metadata, statistically auditable node selection. The source frames this as making targeted attacks expensive and detectable, not impossible, so partial is defensible.
Devices only send to nodes whose attested measurements match an append-only transparency log. Gap: images publish up to 90 days later and only a security-critical subset of source is released.
Requests are encrypted to attested node keys; load balancers and gateways hold no decryption keys, so guarantees don't depend on TLS-terminating components.

keywords_note: Each keyword is a case-insensitive regex; a ledger promise matches when every keyword matches its 'promise' text. A list of verdicts means any of them is accepted.
